opening_message:
Ticket 1: Douglas Salinas (employee ID E045) requests write access to Payroll.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E045.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Douglas Salinas (E045) is a full-time Engineer. Requested write access to Payroll. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin would require owning the system, which does not apply here. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Engineer (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Douglas Salinas (E045) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors without advanced training may have at most read. Requested write exceeds the maximum, so grant read.
reason: Douglas Salinas (E045) requested write access to Payroll. The two agent notes conflict on employment type: one lists full_time (HR/role DB), but the Security agent's note, based on the Security DB, lists the employee as a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors without advanced security training may have at most read access, and write exceeds that maximum. Given the conflicting facts, I grant the safest level consistent with the security-recorded classification: read (the maximum allowed for a contractor with basic training).
